source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Interpret the 1.5-ng/mL level as proof of toxicity and give digoxin immune Fab regardless of symptoms, renal function, or electrolyte status.","B":"Interpret the 1.5-ng/mL level as subtherapeutic and automatically increase the dose without considering the indication or clinical response.","C":"Interpret the 1.5-ng/mL level with symptoms, renal function, electrolytes, and clinical response rather than labeling the isolated value automatically therapeutic or toxic.","D":"Ignore when the level was drawn because the interval between the last digoxin dose and specimen collection does not affect interpretation."}}
source_row.rationale: Digoxin labeling states that an isolated serum concentration should not be used alone to change dosing, provides concentration-risk context, and recommends sampling just before the next dose or at least 6 hours after the last dose.
source_row.source_detail: §2.5 Monitoring to Assess Safety, Efficacy, and Therapeutic Blood Levels. DailyMed label currentness rechecked 2026-08-15. NCSBN first-check: Overview of Content — Reduction of Risk Potential, printed p.13: laboratory/diagnostic interpretation, focused assessment and complication-risk monitoring. 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan; effective 2026-04-01 through 2029-03-31; currentness rechecked 2026-08-15.
source_row.stem: A client taking digoxin has a serum digoxin concentration of 1.5 ng/mL drawn at least 6 hours after the last dose. Which interpretation is most accurate?
